title: The text discusses the oppressive political climate in Zaire under President Mobutu, highlighting the severe restrictions on political opposition, freedom of the press, and the judiciary. Political opponents face expulsion, torture, and imprisonment without trial, with reports of inhumane conditions in prisons. The judiciary lacks independence, and the media is heavily controlled by the government, limiting any criticism of the regime. Overall, the situation reflects a systematic suppression of dissent and human rights violations in Zaire.
